thread.title: Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo
Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) is set to report second quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Monday. And this time, expectations are high, unlike the so-so “conglomerate-esque” results Wall Street has come to expect from the tech giant.
After selling off nearly 5% after reporting first quarter earnings in April, Google shares have come roaring back, surging some 20%. The stock closed Friday at $1,197.88 and has risen about 14% year to date, compared with 4.85% rise for the S&P 500 index. At the same time, however, Google shares have lagged behind its FAANG peers: Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Netflix ( NFLX ). Alphabet returned just 22% in the past 12 months, while its peers have an average of 56% returns in that same span.
The reason for Google’s underperformance has to do with concern about the company’s profit margins, which have been impacted by a combination of factors, including its investments in areas such as the cloud and self-driving vehicles and higher Traffic Acquisition Costs in the advertising business. Bulls argue that the company’s focus on innovation, particularly in the realm of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud and home automation (among others) will be long-term tailwinds for the company. On Monday the management must pitch its case for why more patience is needed.
In the three months that ended June, Wall Street expects the Mountain View, Calif.-based company to earn $9.59 per share on revenue of $32.19 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $5.01 per share on revenue of $26.01 billion. For the full year, ending in December, earnings of $44.20 per share would rise 37% year over year, while full-year revenue of the $136.07 billion would rise 22.7% year over year.
The top and bottom line numbers won’t be the only story here, however. There’s also the issue of European Union’s $5.07 billion Android antitrust fine and the potential impact this could have on the company’s profit. While the company said it planned to appeal the fine, it also disclosed — via an SEC filing — that the fine will be accounted in its Q2 report. This means that potentially more than 70% of Q2 net income could be wiped out.
Its dominance in the digital ad industry, where there’s been no sign of slowing down , will also be an area of focus. The company is positioned to sustain 10%-plus digital ad revenue growth over the next five years as traditional ad content moves to quicker onto internet mediums such as its widely-visited online assets like YouTube.
Will its results support this projection? Elsewhere, analysts will want to see improvements in terms of the Cloud, where it competes with Amazon’s AWS cloud platform and Microsoft’s ( MSFT ) Azure.
Google CEO Sundar Pichai has touted his company’s progress in the Cloud, announcing recently that Google’s Cloud business was producing over $1 billion in revenue each quarter and saying quarterly revenue continues to accelerate. A hint on how much ground Google has made on Amazon and Microsoft could be revealed Monday. And to the extent the Cloud maintains its momentum, this would offset any perceived weakness in other areas of the business.
